newsletters.title: How to Get Better at AI by Asking AI
newsletters.content:
Five prompts that took me from one-off chats to delegating whole projects to teams of agents  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
https://every.?ev_audience=free


HOW TO GET BETTER AT AI BY ASKING AI https://every.?ev_audience=free


FIVE PROMPTS THAT TOOK ME FROM ONE-OFF CHATS TO DELEGATING WHOLE PROJECTS TO TEAMS OF AGENTS https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Arielle Shipper https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.?ev_audience=free to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



For most of my working life, the first step of any task began with a blank slate: an empty Google Doc, a fresh email, or a new Excel spreadsheet. From researching to writing formulas, the banalities of every stage of construction fell to me. AI made that process faster, but the way I accomplished it wasn’t all that different. I started with a new chat and prompted it over and over until the output matched my unspoken definition of “done.”

When I started at Every in May, I was still working that way. When I needed to issue contractor payments, I worked from one chat thread, prompting sequentially to surface agreement terms, approve payment, and send email confirmations that payment had been issued.

Things look very different today. Last week, I needed to verify the cost of purchasing equity for an employee across multiple grants, strike prices, and vesting schedules. Rather than tackle this complex task in a single thread, I split the project among several subagents that coordinated independently to verify information on signed agreements, run the math, double-check it and flag discrepancies, and return a draft of a Slack message that I could approve with a simple “yes.” That work ran on skills, orchestrator threads, context packets, subagents, MCPs, and computer use. It’s a veritable alphabet soup of technical terms that I was previously sure could only be understood and deployed by Highly Technical People, yet I now find myself reaching for these techniques daily, helping me work faster, with better and more precise results that I can be confident about.

I was prompted to make the shift from a tweet. Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free tweeted https://every.?ev_audience=free in June that she had asked Codex where she fell on Mike Taylor https://every.

#### **DIIO**

## [What if AI understood why a conversation was happening?](https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-10-02&utm_term=main_ad_starter)

Caption: Courtesy: Diio

Most AI tools can capture what was said. diio understands what the conversation was trying to accomplish.

diio analyzes customer interactions across meetings, calls, WhatsApp, and other channels, combining the content of the conversation with its context, objective, and your team’s own playbooks.

That lets its AI go beyond summaries. It can identify customer needs, objections, commitments, risks, next steps, and signals that indicate whether an interaction is progressing toward its goal.

The result is a continuously growing intelligence layer built from real conversations — not just notes or structured fields.

Teams can use that intelligence to understand customers, prioritize what needs attention, improve how they execute, and act on signals hidden across thousands of interactions.

diio turns conversations into context AI can understand and context into better decisions.

[Try it for free](https://www.diio.com/us/starter-diio?utm_source=ai_valley&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ai_valley_2026&utm_content=2026-10-02&utm_term=main_ad_starter)

----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: 48% of People Thought This AI Was a Real Human | Introducing Griffin (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lHw6yoyPkpo)

**Tavus built an AI that fooled 48% of people on video calls** - its new [Griffin](https://www.tavus.io/griffin) model can see, hear, talk and react simultaneously during live video calls. Unlike most existing AI video models that take turns speaking, Griffin can watch and listen while it talks. It can nod mid-sentence, handle interruptions, change its facial expressions and even talk about things it sees on your screen.

The result is incredibly convincing. In a study Tavus conducted with 54 people, 48% thought Griffin-Lite was a real human after a one-minute blind video call. Its previous model managed just 2.4%. Griffin also topped NVIDIA's VideoFDB benchmark, scoring 3.83/5 on NVIDIA’s video full-duplex benchmark, compared to 3.92/5 for a real human (that gap is way too small).

While that video call study had a small number of participants and was conducted by Tavaus, the demos are incredibly convincing and make for a grim future for video calls.

As Emad Mostaque [put it](https://x.com/EMostaque/status/2105744708299526243), "remote work is cooked". That might be premature, but imagine getting on a video call with a job candidate, coworker, or someone claiming to be a family member and having no idea whether they're real.

Griffin-Lite is limited to trusted testers for now while Tavus works on safety and disclosure features before a wider release.

The technology is impressive. The potential for scams is equally impressive, unfortunately (good luck trusting video calls in a few years).

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

Generic AI gives everyone the same intelligence. Your Sentience is a high-fidelity digital twin shaped by your memories, relationships, voice, and judgment.

Your Sentience connects the context across your email, calendar, messages, meetings, and documents. It uses that context to prepare you for decisions, write responses you would actually send, and act with your approval. It learns from every correction and continually improves.

Your AI should become more like you, not make you more like everyone else.

----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e54f8f79-be09-40f7-904e-c132c99db5f7/image_-_2026-10-01T200909.002__1_.png?t=1790865418)
Caption: 

**1/ Trump wants the US government to stop calling it AI** - Trump [signed](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-ai-constitution-tech-execs-openai-anthropic-voluntary-controls/) an executive order instructing the US government to refer to AI as “Super Intelligence” (SI) in official communications, websites and policy documents. It doesn’t affect any regulations or contracts that mention AI, but Trump wants the name change “to ensure the American people know this is not your everyday technology.” His top science advisor has 60 days to come up with a proposed federal definition of SI.

Separately, Musk, Zuck, Dario, Jensen, Sundar, Brockman and a bunch of other tech execs signed Trump’s “[morally binding](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/)” AI safety pact. It’s voluntary for now, with companies agreeing to things like safety testing, external audits and board-level oversight. Trump says actual regulation could come later.

Trump also discussed forming a 10-person committee to oversee the effort and said he’d appoint an AI czar in the coming days.

Though it’s gonna take me a minute to start calling it SI.

**2/ OpenAI just had a pretty big DevDay, here’s what’s new:**

[Dots](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2104984504133918973?s=20): your own always-on AI coworkers that run on GPT-6 Astra. They each have their own cloud computer & browser, context, tool access, and can use 4,000+ apps via plugins. You can offload work to a dot, leave, and come back when it’s done or when it needs you. Dots will follow you around and you can use them in ChatGPT, via voice, in Slack/Teams, and soon via text.

[ChatGPT Space](https://x.com/ChatGPT/status/2104986841145602351?s=20): a place where you, your team members, and your agents can all work together, access the same files, and share context.

[GPT-6.1 Sol](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2104986129686741046?s=20): surprisingly close to Astra on coding, computer use, and “professional” tasks, and it’s still $2/$10 per million tokens. 1.05m context window. They’ve also got a new Ultrafast mode, which gets like 300 tokens/sec in Codex.

[Codex](https://x.com/OpenAIDevs/status/2104999323385929777?s=20): can now spin up cloud coding environments so you can code even when your computer is asleep, voice in CLI, parallel agents, code review, and a new security agent that can scan your GitHub repo and prep fixes.

It looks like OpenAI is no longer just building ChatGPT and models, they’re now building agents, computers, workspaces, dev stack, marketplace, etc. etc. It’s a lot.

[Explore OpenAI DevDay 2026](https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap)

**3/ Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon **- [their new flagship model](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-argon/) built for long-running coding, knowledge work and cybersecurity tasks. The ridiculous bit: it can output up to 1 million tokens in a single run, up from 64K before. It also gets 77.9% on DeepSWE and Google says it leads across a bunch of professional-work benchmarks.

It seems to fall behind a bit on some longer technical and scientific tasks (Astra is better at those) and ML eng/terminal tasks (Opus 5.5 is better at those). Some Googlers have apparently expressed concern that Argon benchmarks better at coding than it actually feels in practice, but Google disagrees.

Argon is rolling out to a small group of trusted cyber defenders first, with paid API customers and AI Ultra getting access later.

Also kinda wild: Google says Argon agents already found optimizations that freed 300+ TiB of memory across its own data centers.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------

* [Grok Bot](https://x.com/bot/status/2105373767568621895?s=20) - it can now hand off coding tasks to Cursor, manage your PRs with GitHub and Origin plugins, and share video demos of what they build

* [Ideogram 4.5](https://x.com/ideogram_ai/status/2105327223431737780?s=20) - the most precise image editing model

* [d1](https://x.com/liquidai/status/2105003472332693869?s=20) - a decision model like Jev

* [Runway Ads](https://www.adweek.com/programmatic/runways-ai-video-agent-creates-and-measures-ads-across-platforms) - AI video firm now can connect to a brand’s accounts on Meta, Google, and TikTok

* [Call4me](https://x.com/skeptrune/status/2105320262938009690?s=20) - an ai agent that handles phone calls for you

* [Muse for Small Business](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/29/meta-launches-muse-for-small-business-zuckerberg-pushes-enterprise-ai.html) - Meta has launched a dedicated agent for small business workplaces

A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO COMMODITY INTELLIGENCE, OWNING YOUR AI STACK, AND DECIDING WHEN TO STILL REACH FOR THE FRONTIER https://every.?ev_audience=free

by Kai Zau https://every.?ev_audience=free, Opus 4.6 https://every.?ev_audience=free, GLM 5.1 https://every.?ev_audience=free, and GLM 5.2 https://every.?ev_audience=free

Midjourney/Every illustration.

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

The frontier model you pay for every month can discover new antibiotics—a lot of firepower for summarizing your meeting notes. Kai Zau, a programmer who runs millions of tokens a day through open models on a Mac Studio, has spent years testing where open models are good enough to replace frontier ones. His guide is built around commodity intelligence: the growing set of tasks where open models now match frontier quality for a fraction of the cost. He explains how to pick the right model tier for a job, where to host it, and how to connect it to the tools you already use, including coding agents and automated workflows. If you pay for Claude or ChatGPT and aren’t sure you need to, start here.—Kate Lee https://every.?ev_audience=free
